title: Shree Namasakar Mahamantra

lines.transliteration: Namo Arihantanam
lines.translation_en: I bow to the Arihants

lines.transliteration: Namo Siddhanam
lines.translation_en: I bow to the Siddhas

lines.transliteration: Namo Ayariyanam
lines.translation_en: I bow to the Acharyas

lines.transliteration: Namo Uvajjhayanam
lines.translation_en: I bow to the Upadhyayas

lines.transliteration: Namo Loe Savva Sahunam
lines.translation_en: I bow to all the Sadhus in the world

lines.transliteration: Eso Pancha Namukkaro
lines.translation_en: These five salutations

lines.transliteration: Savva Pavappanasano
lines.translation_en: Are the destroyer of all sins

lines.transliteration: Mangalanam Cha Savvesim
lines.translation_en: And among all auspicious things

lines.transliteration: Padhamam Havai Mangalam
lines.translation_en: This is the first and foremost auspicious

interpretation: By this sutra, obeisance is offered to the five supreme beings — the Arihants (living liberated ones), the Siddhas (fully liberated souls), the Acharyas (spiritual leaders), the Upadhyayas (scripture teachers), and the Sadhus (monks and nuns). These five salutations together destroy all sins and karmas, and are declared to be the most auspicious of all auspicious things in the three worlds.

title: Shree Panchindiya Sootra

lines.transliteration: Panchindiya Samvarano
lines.translation_en: One who restrains the five senses

lines.transliteration: Taha Navaviha Bambhachera Guttidharo
lines.translation_en: Who observes the nine types of celibacy

lines.transliteration: Chauviha Kasaya Mukko
lines.translation_en: Who is free from the four passions

lines.transliteration: Ia Attharasa Gunehi Samjutto
lines.translation_en: And is endowed with eighteen qualities

lines.transliteration: Pancha Mahavvaya Jutto
lines.translation_en: Who is equipped with the five great vows

lines.transliteration: Pancha Vihayara Palana Samattho
lines.translation_en: Who is capable of observing the five ways of conduct

lines.transliteration: Pancha Samio Tigutto
lines.translation_en: Who observes five carefulness and three controls

lines.transliteration: Chhatteesa Guno Guroo Majjha
lines.translation_en: Such a Guru possesses thirty-six qualities

interpretation: This sutra describes the thirty-six qualities of Shri Acharya Maharaja — including restraint of the five senses, nine types of celibacy, freedom from the four passions, the five great vows, five carefulness and three controls. It is uttered to consecrate the Sthapanacharya at the beginning of any sacred rite.

title: Shree Khamasamana Sootra

lines.transliteration: Ichchhami Khamasamano
lines.translation_en: I wish to offer obeisance

lines.transliteration: Vandium Javanijjae
lines.translation_en: Having bowed, with permission granted

lines.transliteration: Niseehiae Matthaenam Vandami
lines.translation_en: With restraint, I salute with my head bowed

interpretation: This sutra is uttered while offering obeisance to Lord Jineshvara and the Shramana. It expresses the devotee's sincere wish to bow with proper permission and humility, surrendering the ego completely.

title: Shree Abbhutthio Sootra

lines.transliteration: icchä-kärena sandisaha bhagavan !
lines.translation_en: O Respected Guru Maharaj, I ask for your permission

lines.transliteration: abbhutthiomi, abbhintara-devasiam khämeum?
lines.translation_en: I wish to ask forgiveness for the transgressions of the day

lines.transliteration: iccham, khämemi devasiam.
lines.translation_en: Yes, I ask forgiveness for the day

lines.transliteration: jam kinci apattiam, para-pattiam; bhatte, päne;
lines.translation_en: For any fault in serving food or water, whether my fault or caused by others

lines.transliteration: vinae, veyävacce; äläve, samläve; uccäsane, samäsane; antara-bhäsäe, uvari-bhäsäe; jam kinci majjha
lines.translation_en: For not caring for you properly, for disrespecting you by sitting higher or at the same level, for interrupting or talking back to you

lines.transliteration: vinaya-parihinam, suhumam vä, bäyaram vä;
lines.translation_en: For any impoliteness shown, whether subtle or obvious

lines.transliteration: tubbhe jänaha, aham na jänämi;
lines.translation_en: What you know of my faults, I may not even be aware of myself

lines.transliteration: tassa micchä mi dukkadam
lines.translation_en: For all of those wrongdoings, I beg your pardon

interpretation: By means of this sutra, the devotee asks forgiveness for any impoliteness or improper conduct shown towards the Guru Maharaja — whether known or unknown, intentional or unintentional, in food, water, service, speech or action.

title: Shree Iriyavahiyam Sootra

lines.transliteration: Ichchhä-kärena Sandisaha Bhagavan, Iryä Vahiyanm Paddikka-mämi? Ichchham Ichchämi Padikkamiu.
lines.translation_en: With your permission, O Lord, may I repent for the sins committed while walking? Yes, I desire to repent.

lines.transliteration: Iriyä vahiyäe, Virähanäe,
lines.translation_en: For the violations and harm caused while walking,

lines.transliteration: Gamanä-gamane,
lines.translation_en: During coming and going,

lines.transliteration: Pänakka-mane, Biakka-mane, Hariyakka-mane, Osä-Uttinga, Panaga-daga, Matti Makkadä, Santäna, Sankamane.
lines.translation_en: For harm to living beings in water, in seeds, in green plants, in dew, in ant hills, in moss, in water bodies, in earth, in spider webs, while crossing.

lines.transliteration: Je me jivä virähiyä,
lines.translation_en: Whatever living beings may have been hurt by me,

lines.transliteration: Egindiyä, Beindiyä, Teindiyä, Chaurindiyä, Panchindiyä,
lines.translation_en: Beings with one sense, two senses, three senses, four senses, or five senses,

lines.transliteration: Abihayä, Vattiyä, Lesiyä, Sanghäiyä, Sanghattiyä, Pariyaviyä, Kilämiyä, Uddaviyä, Thänäo-Thänam, Sankämiyä,
lines.translation_en: Those I struck, covered with dust, rubbed against, made to collide, inflicted pain upon, frightened, tilted, turned upside down, or shifted from place to place,

lines.transliteration: Jiviyäo-vavaroviyä,
lines.translation_en: Those I separated from life and made lifeless,

lines.transliteration: Tassa Michchhä Mi Dukkadam.
lines.translation_en: May all that be forgiven and may those sins be dissolved.

interpretation: This sutra seeks repentance for the unintentional harm caused to any living beings while walking, moving, coming or going. Jainism recognizes that even daily movement can harm tiny organisms, and this sutra expresses deep remorse for such unavoidable harm, reinforcing the principle of Ahimsa (non-violence).

title: Shree Tassa-Uttaree Sootra

lines.transliteration: Tassa Uttaree Karanaenam
lines.translation_en: For the purpose of further atonement

lines.transliteration: Payachchhitta Karanaenam
lines.translation_en: For the purpose of penance

lines.transliteration: Visohi Karanaenam
lines.translation_en: For the purpose of purification

lines.transliteration: Visalli Karanaenam
lines.translation_en: For removing the dart of sin

lines.transliteration: Pavanam Kammanam Nigghayanatthae
lines.translation_en: For the annihilation of sinful karmas

lines.transliteration: Thami Kaaussaggam
lines.translation_en: I undertake Kayotsarga

interpretation: This sutra introduces the Kayotsarga meditation by stating five purposes: atonement, penance, purification, removal of the dart of sin, and annihilation of sinful karmas. It is recited before entering the still meditation posture, preparing the mind and body for deep spiritual practice.

title: Shree Annattha Sootra

lines.transliteration: Annattha Oosasienam Neesasienam
lines.translation_en: Except for breathing in and breathing out

lines.transliteration: Khasienam Chheienam Jambhaienam
lines.translation_en: Except for coughing, sneezing and yawning

lines.transliteration: Udduenam Vayanisaggenam
lines.translation_en: Except for releasing gas and natural body release

lines.transliteration: Bhamalee Pittamuchchhae
lines.translation_en: Except for dizziness and nausea

lines.transliteration: Suhumehin Anga Sanchalehin
lines.translation_en: Except for subtle movements of the limbs

lines.transliteration: Suhumehin Khela Sanchalehin
lines.translation_en: Except for subtle movements of saliva

lines.transliteration: Suhumehin Ditthi Sanchalehin
lines.translation_en: Except for subtle movements of the eyes

lines.transliteration: Evamaiehim Agarehim Abhaggo Avirahio Hujja Me Kaaussaggo
lines.translation_en: With these exemptions, may my Kayotsarga remain unbroken and undisturbed

lines.transliteration: Java Arihantanam Bhagavantanam Namukkarenam Na Paremi
lines.translation_en: Until I complete the Navkar salutation to the Arihant Bhagavants

lines.transliteration: Tava Kayam Thanaenam Monenam Jhanenam Appanam Vosirami
lines.translation_en: Until then I remain in stillness, silence and meditation, relinquishing the body

interpretation: This sutra lists the sixteen natural bodily exemptions that do not break the Kayotsarga meditation — breathing, coughing, sneezing, and subtle involuntary movements. It establishes the proper decorum for performing Kayotsarga with firmness, committing to remain still and silent until the Navkar Mantra recitation is complete.

title: Shree Logassa Sootra

lines.transliteration: Logassa Ujjoagare Dhamma Titthayare Jine
lines.translation_en: The Jinas who are the illuminators of the world and founders of dharma

lines.transliteration: Arihante Kittaissam Chauveesam Pi Kevali
lines.translation_en: I glorify the twenty-four omniscient Arihants

lines.transliteration: Usabha Majiam Cha Vande Sambhava Abhinandanam Cha Sumaim Cha
lines.translation_en: I bow to Rushabha and Ajita; I bow to Sambhava, Abhinandana and Sumati

lines.transliteration: Paumappaham Suvasam Jinam Cha Chandappaham Vande
lines.translation_en: I bow to Padmaprabha, Suparshva and Chandraprabha

lines.transliteration: Suvihi Cha Puppadantam Seetal Sijjans Vasupujjam Cha
lines.translation_en: I bow to Suvidhina, Shitala, Shreyansa and Vasupujya

lines.transliteration: Vimalamanantam Cha Jinam Dhammam Santim Cha Vandami
lines.translation_en: I bow to Vimala, Ananta, Dharma and Shanti

lines.transliteration: Kunthu Aram Cha Mallim Vande Munisuvvayam Namijinam Cha
lines.translation_en: I bow to Kunthu, Ara, Malli, Munisuvrata and Nami

lines.transliteration: Vandami Ritthanemim Pasam Taha Vaddhamanam Cha
lines.translation_en: I bow to Neminatha, Parshvanatha and Vardhamana

lines.transliteration: Evam Mae Abhithuya Vihuya Rayamala Pahina Jaramarana Chauveesam Pi Jinavara Titthayara Me Paseeyantu
lines.translation_en: Thus glorified by me — may these twenty-four Jina lords, freed from passion, age and death, be gracious unto me

lines.transliteration: Kittiya Vandiya Mahiya Je E Logassa Uttama Siddha Arugga Bohilabham Samahi Vara Muttamam Dintu
lines.translation_en: The praised and honored Siddhas — may they grant us good health, enlightenment and the highest Samadhi

lines.transliteration: Chandesu Nimmalayara Aichchesu Ahiyam Payasayara Sagaravara Gambhira Siddha Siddhim Mama Disantu
lines.translation_en: Purer than the moon, brighter than the sun, deeper than the great ocean — may the Siddhas show me liberation

interpretation: The Logassa Sutra glorifies all twenty-four Tirthankaras by name, from Rushabhadeva to Mahavira, and all Siddhas of the three phases of time. It offers a prayer for the attainment of salvation through the three gems of right faith, right knowledge and right conduct — asking the liberated souls for good health, spiritual enlightenment and the highest state of meditation.

title: Shree Karemi-Bhante Sootra

lines.transliteration: Karemi Bhante Samaiyam
lines.translation_en: O Lord, I undertake Samayika

lines.transliteration: Savajjam Jogam Pachchhakkhami
lines.translation_en: I renounce all sinful activities

lines.transliteration: Java Niyamam Pajjuvasami
lines.translation_en: As long as I observe this vow I remain in restraint

lines.transliteration: Duviham Tivihenam Manenam Vayae Kaenam
lines.translation_en: In two ways and three ways — by mind, speech and body

lines.transliteration: Na Karemi Na Karavemi
lines.translation_en: I will not do sin, nor cause others to do sin

lines.transliteration: Tassa Bhante Padikkamami Nindami Garihami
lines.translation_en: O Lord, I repent, I condemn, I confess

lines.transliteration: Appanam Vosirami
lines.translation_en: I relinquish my ego

interpretation: The Karemi Bhante Sutra is the formal vow of Samayika — a 48-minute period of complete equanimity. The practitioner vows to renounce all sinful activities of mind, speech and body, neither committing nor causing others to commit any harm. It concludes with repentance for past sins and a surrender of the ego, placing the soul in a monk-like state for the duration of the Samayika.

title: Shree Samaiya Vayajutto Sootra

lines.transliteration: sämäiya-vaya-jutto, jäva mane hoi niyama-sanjutto. chinnai asuham kammam, samäiya jattiä värä.
lines.translation_en: One who observes Sämäyik and keeps the mind restrained destroys inauspicious karma for as long as they remain in Sämäyik.

lines.transliteration: sämäiyammi u kae, samano iva sävao havai jamhä. eena käranenam, bahuso sämäiyam kujjä.
lines.translation_en: As long as the aspirant observes Sämäyik, he/she is as good as a monk; therefore Sämäyik should be performed frequently.

lines.transliteration: sämäyika vidhi se liyä, vidhi se purna kiyä, vidhi mem jo koi avidhi hui ho, una sabakä mana-vacana-käyä se micchä mi dukkadam.
lines.translation_en: I took the vow of Sämäyik according to the prescribed method and shall also end it accordingly. If I deviated from the prescribed method mentally, verbally, or physically, may all that be forgiven.

lines.transliteration: dasa mana ke, dasa vacana ke, bäraha käyä ke — ina battisa dosna mem se jo koi dosha lagä ho, una sabakä mana-vacana-käyä se micchä mi dukkadam.
lines.translation_en: There are 10 faults of mind, 10 faults of speech, and 12 faults of body. If I have indulged in any of these 32 faults mentally, verbally, or physically, may all that be forgiven.

interpretation: This sutra reveals the profound spiritual significance of Samayika. During the practice, a layperson attains the spiritual status equivalent to a monk or nun, and every performance cuts off inauspicious karmas. The sutra encourages performing Samayika as frequently as possible and closes with seeking forgiveness for any faults.

title: Shree Jaga Chintamani Sootra

lines.transliteration: Jaga – Cinta – Mani ! Jaga – Naha ! Jaga – Guru ! Jaga – Rakkhana ! Jaga – Bandhava !
lines.translation_en: Oh Tirthankar Bhagawan, you are the best jewel of the universe. You are the ultimate head, preceptor, protector, and elder brother of the whole universe.

lines.transliteration: Jaga – Sattha – Vaha ! Jaga – Bhava – Viakkhana ! Attha – Vaya – Santhavia – Ruva !
lines.translation_en: You are the guide of the entire universe and you perceive all inner thoughts. Your idols are consecrated on Mt. Ashtpad.

lines.transliteration: Kammattha Vinasana ! Cauvisampi Jina – Vara ! Jayantu A-Ppadihaya – Sasana !
lines.translation_en: You have eradicated all eight categories of Karma. Oh Twenty-four Tirthankaras, may the four-fold Jain order you established prevail unobstructed forever.

lines.transliteration: Kamma – Bhumihim Kamma – Bhumihim Padhama – Sanghayani Ukkosaya Sattari – Saya. Jina – Varana Viharanta Labbhai ;
lines.translation_en: In all Karma Bhumis, at any time, a maximum of 170 Jineshvar Bhagawan with the most unique physique may exist at once.

lines.transliteration: Nava – Kodihim Kevalina , Kodi – Sahassa Nava Sahu Gammai . Sampai Jina – Vara Visa Muni , Bihum Kodihim Vara – Nana; Samanaha Kodi – Sahassa – Dua , Thunijjai Nicca Vihani .
lines.translation_en: 90 million omniscients and 90,000 million monks may exist. I pray every morning to the 20 current Tirthankaras, 20 million omniscient monks, and 20,000 million other monks.

lines.transliteration: Jayau Samiya Jayau Samiya Risaha Sattunji , Ujjinti Pahu-Nemi-Jina , Jayau Vira Saccauri – Mandana ,
lines.translation_en: Oh Lord, you are great, you are great. Bhagawan Rushabhadev graces Mt. Shatrunjay; Neminath Bhagawan graces Mt. Girnar; Bhagawan Mahavir-swami graces the temple of Sachori.

lines.transliteration: Mahuri – Pasa Duha – Duria – Khandana , Avara – Videhim Tittha – Yara , Cihum Disi Vidisi Jim Kevi , Tianagaya Sampai Ya , Vandum Jina Savve Vi .
lines.translation_en: Bhagawan Parshvanath of Mathura eradicates suffering and sin. I offer obeisance to all Jineshvar Bhagawan — past, present, and future — in all directions of the universe.

lines.transliteration: Satta – Navai Sahassa , Lakkha Chappanna Attha – Kodio . Battisa – Saya Basiyaim , Tia Loe Ceie Vande .
lines.translation_en: I bow down to the 85,700,232 temples present throughout the three realms of the universe.

lines.transliteration: Panarasa – Kodi – Sayaim , Kodi Bayala Lakkha Adavanna , Chattisa – Sahassa – Asiim , Sasaya – Bimbaim Panamami .
lines.translation_en: I bow down to the 15,425,836,080 eternal Tirthankar idols present in the universe.

interpretation: This Chaitya-Vandana composed by Shri Gautama Swami glorifies all Tirthankara Bhagavants and describes the vast numbers of Jina idols and pilgrimage places across the three worlds. It opens with six beautiful epithets for the Lord and concludes with a prayer for the victory of the unobstructed Jain teachings.

title: Shree Jan Kin Chi Sootra

lines.transliteration: Jankinchi Nama Tittham
lines.translation_en: Whatever Jina pilgrimage centers exist by name

lines.transliteration: Sagge Payali Manuse Loe
lines.translation_en: In heaven, the nether world, or the human world

lines.transliteration: Jaim Jina Bimbhaim Taim Savvaim Vandami
lines.translation_en: All those Jina idols — I salute every single one of them

interpretation: By this sutra, salutation is offered universally to every Jaina pilgrimage center and Jina idol existing anywhere in the three worlds. The devotee transcends physical limitations, offering reverence to every temple simultaneously through pure intention.

title: Shree Namutthunam Sootra

lines.transliteration: Namotthunam arihantanam bhagavantanam aigaranam
lines.translation_en: Obeisance to all the Arihantas, the magnificent, founders of the path.

lines.transliteration: Titthayaranam sayamsambuddhanam purisuttamanam, purisasihanam
lines.translation_en: Founders of the religion, self-enlightened, great amongst men, lions amongst men.

lines.transliteration: Purisavarapundariyanam purisavaragandhahatthinam
lines.translation_en: Lotuses amongst men, fragrant elephants amongst men.

lines.transliteration: Loguttamanam loganahanam, loga hianam
lines.translation_en: Exalted in the world, masters of the world, benefactors of the world.

lines.transliteration: Logapaivanam logapajjoagaranam
lines.translation_en: Lamps of the world and its light.

lines.transliteration: Abhayadayanam cakkhudayanam maggadayanam saranadayanam
lines.translation_en: Granters of fearlessness, givers of eyesight, guides of the true path and providers of shelter.

lines.transliteration: Jivadayanam bohidayanam
lines.translation_en: Givers of life, granters of enlightenment.

lines.transliteration: Dhammadayanam dhammadesanayam dhammanayaganam dhammasarahinam
lines.translation_en: Givers of dharma, givers of sermon, heroes of the dharma and its charioteers.

lines.transliteration: Dhammavara cauranta cakkavattinam
lines.translation_en: Destroyers of the four modes of rebirth, great emperors of religion.

lines.transliteration: Divottanam saranagai paittha appadihayavara nanadamsanadharanam
lines.translation_en: Islands for those drowning in the ocean of transmigration, givers of shelter against rebirth, givers of prestige, holders of indestructible knowledge and perception.

lines.transliteration: Viattha chaumanam jinanam javayanam
lines.translation_en: Free of non-omniscience, victors, granters of victory.

lines.transliteration: Tinnanam tarayanam buddhanam bohayanam muttanam moyaganam
lines.translation_en: Omniscient ones who help others cross the ocean of transmigration; enlightened ones who spread enlightenment; free ones who help others attain freedom.

lines.transliteration: Savvanunam savvadarisinam sivam ayalam aruam anantam akkhayam avvabaham
lines.translation_en: All-knowing, all-seeing, auspicious, immovable, free from all disease, endless, indestructible, unimpeded.

lines.transliteration: Apunaravittim siddhigainamadheyam thanam sampattanam
lines.translation_en: Free from the cycle of transmigration, attainers of the state of existence known as Siddhahood.

lines.transliteration: Namo jinanam jiyabhayanam
lines.translation_en: Obeisance to the Jinas, who have conquered fear itself.

interpretation: By this sutra, Shakrendra (king of gods) glorifies Lord Arihanta with an extensive list of superior qualities and epithets — celebrating their role as supreme guides, protectors and enlighteners of all living beings across the three worlds.

title: Shree Javanti Cheiaim Sootra

lines.transliteration: Javanti Cheiim Uddhe A Ahe A Tiriyaloe A
lines.translation_en: All the Jina temples that exist — in the upper, lower and middle worlds

lines.transliteration: Savvaim Taim Vande
lines.translation_en: I offer salutation to all of them

lines.transliteration: Iha Santo Tattha Santaim
lines.translation_en: Being present here in spirit and there in form

interpretation: By this sutra, salutation is offered to all Jina temples across the three worlds. The devotee transcends physical limitations, offering reverence to every temple simultaneously through pure intention and devotion.

title: Shree Javanta Kevi Sahoo Sootra

lines.transliteration: Javanta Ke Vi Sahoo
lines.translation_en: To all the Sadhus who are living

lines.transliteration: Bharaheravaya Mahavidehe A
lines.translation_en: In the regions of Bharata, Airavata and Mahavidha

lines.transliteration: Savvesim Tesim Panao
lines.translation_en: I bow to all of them

lines.transliteration: Tivihenam Tidanda Virayenam
lines.translation_en: With three-fold restraint, having given up the three rods of body, speech and mind

interpretation: By means of this sutra, obeisance is offered to all the Shramanas present across all regions of the universe — Bharata, Airavata and Mahavidha Kshetra — honoring their complete triple restraint of body, speech and mind.

title: Shree Pancha-Parameshthi Namaskar Sootra

lines.transliteration: Namo Arhat Siddhacharya Upadhyaya Sarvasadhubhyah
lines.translation_en: Salutation to the Arhats, Siddhas, Acharyas, Upadhyayas and all Sadhus

interpretation: By means of this sutra excerpted from the Poorva scripture by Shri Siddhasena Divakara Soori, obeisance is offered simultaneously to all five Parameshthi — the five supreme beings of the Jain faith — in a single, complete Sanskrit salutation.

title: Shree Uvasaggaharam Sootra

lines.transliteration: Uvasaggaharam Päsam, Päsam Vandämi Kamma-ghan-mukkam; Visahar-vis-ninnäsam, Mangal Kallän Äväsam.
lines.translation_en: I bow to Lord Parshwanath, who is attended by the distress removing Parshwa deity, who is free from all types of Karma, who is the destroyer of the poisonous defilements and who is the abode of bliss and well being.

lines.transliteration: Visahar-fuling Manatam, Kanthe Dharei Jo Sayä Manuo; Tassa Gah Rog Märi, Duttha-Jarä Janti Uvasämam.
lines.translation_en: If one always holds in his neck the charm of Visaharfulling, his evil planetary effects, disease, epidemics and acute fever are calmed down.

lines.transliteration: Chitthau Dure Manto, Tujza Panamo Vi Bahu-falo Hoi; Naratiriesu Vi Jivä, Pävanti Na Dukkha-Dogachcham.
lines.translation_en: Let aside that charm, obeisance to you alone would be highly fruitful; thereby humans and animals too would not get misery or evil state.

lines.transliteration: Tuha Sammatte Laddhe, Chintämani Kappa-Päyavabbhahie; Pävanti Avigghenam, Jivä Ayaramaram Thänam.
lines.translation_en: By gaining the right perception laid by you, which is superior to the desire-yielding jewel and the desire-yielding tree, souls easily attain the unaging, immortal state.

lines.transliteration: Ea Santhuo Mahäyas, Bhatti-bbhar-nibbharen Hiyaenam; Tä Dev Dijza Bohim, Bhave Bhave Päs Jinachanda.
lines.translation_en: Oh highly esteemable Lord, I have thus prayed to you with a heart flowing with devotion; hence Omniscient Parshwa Lord, bestow wisdom upon me in every life.

interpretation: Composed by Shri Bhadra Bahu Swami, this stotra glorifies Lord Parshvanatha as the supreme remover of all obstacles — physical, spiritual and karmic. It is especially recited for protection from disease, evil forces and calamities. The stotra expresses complete surrender and devotion to Parshvanatha across all lifetimes, asking for the ultimate gift of enlightenment.

title: Shree Jaya Veeyaraya Sootra

lines.transliteration: jaya viyaräya ! jaga-guru! hou mamam tuha ppabhävao bhayavam! bhava-nivveo maggä-nusäriä, ittha phala siddhi.
lines.translation_en: Hail! O Passionless Lord! Preceptor of the world, through your grace, blessed lord, may I wish for disgust towards the cycle of birth and death, pursuit of the right path and attainment of ultimate bliss.

lines.transliteration: loga-viruddha-chchäo, guru-jana-puä, parattha-karanam cha, suha-guru-jogo tavvayana-sevanä ä-bhavamakhandä.
lines.translation_en: Abandonment of whatever is wrong and impure in the world, respect for the spiritual guide and elders, to be helpful to others, close association with the right spiritual guide and full obedience to his words throughout all worldly existences.

lines.transliteration: värijjai jai vi, niyäna-bandhanam, viya-räya tuha samaye; taha vi mama hujja sevä, bhave bhave tumha chalanänam.
lines.translation_en: O Passionless lord! Even though in your doctrine it is prohibited to ask favors from Jinas, still grant me to serve at your feet in all my worldly existences.

lines.transliteration: dukkha-khao kamma-khao, samähi-maranam cha, bohiläbho a, sampajjau maha eam, tuha näha! panäma-karanenam.
lines.translation_en: O master! By paying obeisance to you, I gain these four favors: unhappiness is destroyed, karmas are destroyed, and right faith and the vow of holy death are acquired.

lines.transliteration: sarva mangala mängalyam, sarva kalyäna kärnam pradhänam sarva dharmänäm, jainam jayati shäsanam.
lines.translation_en: Let the holiest among all, the most prosperous among all, supreme among all religions — the Holy law of Jina — be triumphant.

interpretation: This sutra offers the most complete spiritual prayer in Pratikraman — asking the Veetaraga Lord for every essential element of the path: detachment, right guidance, good company, destruction of karma, peaceful death, and enlightenment. It concludes with a declaration of the supremacy and eternal victory of the Jain teachings.

title: Shree Arihanta Cheiyanam Sootra

lines.transliteration: Arihanta Cheiyenam Karemi Kaaussaggam
lines.translation_en: I perform Kayotsarga for the adoration of Arihanta idols

lines.transliteration: Vandana Vattiaye Puyana Vattiaye
lines.translation_en: For the purpose of salutation and worship

lines.transliteration: Sakkara Vattiaye Sammana Vattiaye
lines.translation_en: For the purpose of honor and respect

lines.transliteration: Bohilabha Vattiaye Niruvasagga Vattiaye
lines.translation_en: For attainment of enlightenment and removal of obstacles

lines.transliteration: Saddhaae Mehaae Dhiiaae Dharanae Anuppehae Vaddhamanieae
lines.translation_en: With faith, with devotion, with steadiness, with holding, with contemplation, with growth

lines.transliteration: Thami Kaaussaggam
lines.translation_en: I undertake Kayotsarga

interpretation: This sutra describes the complete set of emotions and intentions while performing Kayotsarga before the Jina idols. It lists six purposes — salutation, worship, honor, respect, enlightenment and removal of obstacles — and six inner qualities that must accompany the meditation, making it a deeply intentional spiritual practice.

title: Shree Kallana–Kandam Stuti

lines.transliteration: Kallayanakandham Padhamam Jinindham Santim Tao Nemijinam Munindham
lines.translation_en: The root of all auspiciousness — first Jina Rushabhadeva, then Shantinatha, then Nemijina the lord of monks

lines.transliteration: Pasam Payasam Sugunikkathnam Bhattiei Vande Siri Vaddhamanam
lines.translation_en: Parshvanatha of excellent qualities — and with devotion I bow to Shri Vardhamana

lines.transliteration: Apara Samsara Samudda Param Patta Sivam Dintu Suikka Saram
lines.translation_en: Having crossed the limitless ocean of worldly existence, those who attained liberation — may they grant us the pure essence of well-being

lines.transliteration: Savve Jininda Suravinda Vanda Kallyana Valline Visala Kanda
lines.translation_en: All Jinas worshipped by Indra — the great root of auspiciousness, the vast stem of the creeper of welfare

lines.transliteration: Nimmana Magge Varajana Kappam Panasiya Sesa Kuvai Dappam
lines.translation_en: On the path to liberation, the best among men, destroying the pride of all remaining false knowledge

lines.transliteration: Mayam Jinanam Saranam Buhanam Namami Nichcham Tijagappahanum
lines.translation_en: I take refuge in the Jinas, the wise ones — I bow always to the lords of the three worlds

lines.transliteration: kundindu-go-kkhiratusara-vannä, saroja-hatthä kamle nisannä;
lines.translation_en: Fair complexion like jasmine flower, full moon, milk of cow and dew, seated on a lotus, holding lotus in one hand,

lines.transliteration: väesiri putthaya-vagga-hatthä, suhäya sä amha sayä pastthä.
lines.translation_en: And a bundle of books in the other hand, beneficent to all, you — Goddess of learning (Saraswati Devi) — always bless us with happiness.

interpretation: This stuti glorifies five key Tirthankaras — Rushabhadeva, Shantinatha, Neminatha, Parshvanatha and Mahavira — then extends the glorification to all twenty-four Jinas. It celebrates the knowledge of the scriptures and honors the goddess of learning, forming a complete devotional hymn that praises the path from worldly existence to liberation.

title: Shree Sansaradavanala Stuti

lines.transliteration: Samsaradavanala Daha Niram Sammoha Dhooli Harane Samira
lines.translation_en: Like water quenching the forest fire of worldly existence, like wind dispersing the dust of delusion

lines.transliteration: Mayarasa Darana Sara Siram Namami Viram Girisara Dhiram
lines.translation_en: Like the pure stream cutting through maya — I bow to Mahavira, firm as a mountain

lines.transliteration: Bhavavanaama Sura Danava Manavena Choola Vilola Kamalavali Malitani
lines.translation_en: The lotus garlands swayed by gods, demons and humans and offered with devotion

lines.transliteration: Sampurita Abhinata Loka Sameehitani Kamam Namami Jinaraja Padani Tani
lines.translation_en: Fulfilling all the desires of the world — I bow to the feet of the Jinaraja

lines.transliteration: Bodhagatham Supada Padavee Nirapoorabhi Ramam Jivahimsa Viralalaharee Sangamagaha Deham
lines.translation_en: Deep in knowledge, beautiful in conduct, the body immersed in the rare stream of non-violence

lines.transliteration: chula-velam guru-gamamani-sankulam dura-päram,
lines.translation_en: Whose body is vast due to the mutual union of waves of non-violence and simplicity,

lines.transliteration: Saram Veera Gama Jalanidhi Sadaram Sadhu Seve
lines.translation_en: I reverently serve the Sadhu — the essence who has crossed the ocean of Mahavira's path

lines.transliteration: ä-mulä-lola-dhuli-bahula-pari-malä-lidhalolä-limälä,
lines.translation_en: O Goddess Saraswati! With extremely beautiful complexion, and a fragrance so divine that flocks of wasps are drawn to hover around you,

lines.transliteration: jhankäräräva-särä-mala-dala-kamalä-gära-bhumi-niväse!
lines.translation_en: Seated upon a lotus flower whose petals hum with the buzzing of bees,

lines.transliteration: chhäyäsambhära-säre! vara-kamala-kare! tära-härä-bhiräme!
lines.translation_en: Radiant with glorious splendour, holding a lotus flower in one hand, adorned with sparkling necklaces,

lines.transliteration: vänisandoha-dehe! bhava-viraha-varam dehi me devi! säram.
lines.translation_en: O Goddess of speech and learning! Grant me the ultimate blessing — liberation, the final release from all mundane existence.

interpretation: This dual Sanskrit-Prakrit eulogy composed by Shri Haribhadra Soori glorifies Mahaveer Swami, all Jinas, Jinagama and Shruta Devi (goddess of knowledge). The opening verses use vivid natural metaphors — fire, wind and stream — to describe how Mahavira's teachings quench the suffering of worldly life and dispel the delusion of maya.

title: Shree Ichchhakar Sootra

lines.transliteration: Ichchhakara Suharaee
lines.translation_en: With willingness, I ask of your wellbeing

lines.transliteration: Sukha Tapa Shareera Nirabadha
lines.translation_en: Is your penance comfortable? Is your body free from trouble?

lines.transliteration: Sukha Sanjama Jatra Nirvaho Chho Jee
lines.translation_en: Are you able to maintain your vows comfortably?

lines.transliteration: Swami Shata Chhejee
lines.translation_en: O Master, are you well?

lines.transliteration: Bhata Paneeno Labha Dejo Jee
lines.translation_en: Please grant us the privilege of offering food and water

interpretation: By this sutra, the devotee asks the Guru Maharaja about their welfare in all ways — the comfort of their penance, the health of their body, and the maintenance of their vows. An entreaty is also made to accept food and water as an act of devoted service.

title: Shree Pukkharavara Sootra

lines.transliteration: Pukkhara-vara-diva-ddhe, dhayai-sande a jambu-dive a
lines.translation_en: In the best island Pushkaradvipa, in Dhatakikhanda, and in Jambudvipa

lines.transliteration: Bharaheravaya-videhe, dhammei-gare namamsami
lines.translation_en: In Bharata, Airavata and Videha — I bow to the founders of dharma

lines.transliteration: Tama-timira-padala-viddham-sanassa
lines.translation_en: That which destroys the veil of darkness of ignorance

lines.transliteration: Sura-gana-narinda-mahiassa
lines.translation_en: Adored by celestial beings and kings

lines.transliteration: Sima-dharassa vande
lines.translation_en: I worship the sacred doctrine containing the rules of conduct

lines.transliteration: Papphodia-moha-jalassa
lines.translation_en: That which tears apart the net of delusion

lines.transliteration: Jai-jara-marana-soga-panasanassa
lines.translation_en: That which ends the sorrows of birth, old age, and death

lines.transliteration: Kallana-pukkha-lavisala-suha-vahassa
lines.translation_en: That which brings the full and ample bliss of final release

lines.transliteration: Ko deva-danava-narinda-gana-chchiassa
lines.translation_en: Worshiped by gods, demons and kings

lines.transliteration: Dhammassa sara-muva labbha kare pamayam?
lines.translation_en: How can one who understands its essence ever become careless?

lines.transliteration: Siddhe bho! Payao namo jina-mae
lines.translation_en: O people! Pay salutations to the Holy Writ of Lord Tirthankara

lines.transliteration: Nandi saya sanjame
lines.translation_en: Which is proven most beneficial in the path of right conduct

lines.transliteration: devam näga-suvanna-kinnara-gana-ssabbhua-bhävachchie,
lines.translation_en: Which is faithfully worshiped by empyrean gods (vaimänik deva), mansion dwelling gods (bhavana pati deva), luminous gods (jyotishika deva) and forest gods (vyantara deva),

lines.transliteration: logo jattha paitthio jagaminam telukka-machchäsuram,
lines.translation_en: Let this sacred doctrine — which includes a detailed description of all six substances, all three worlds and the living beings therein — be triumphant.

lines.transliteration: Dhammo vaddhau sasao vijayao
lines.translation_en: Let this sacred doctrine be triumphant and victorious

lines.transliteration: Dhammuttram vaddhau
lines.translation_en: May it prosper the dignity of all tenets

lines.transliteration: Suassa bhagavao karemi kassaggam vanda-navattiyae
lines.translation_en: O Lord! To worship the Holy Writ, I will practice the body-abandonment posture

interpretation: This sutra is a hymn in praise of Jain dharma and the Tirthankars residing in the two and a half islands (Adhai Dvip). It glorifies the sacred doctrine as the destroyer of ignorance and delusion, the ender of birth, death and sorrow, and the bringer of supreme bliss. It calls upon all beings — gods, demons and humans — to recognize the priceless essence of this dharma and never be careless about it.

title: Shree Siddhanam Buddhanam Sootra

lines.transliteration: Siddhanam Buddhanam
lines.translation_en: To the Siddhas, the enlightened ones

lines.transliteration: Para-gayanam Parampara-gayanam
lines.translation_en: Who have crossed over, who have gone beyond in succession

lines.transliteration: Loagga-muvagayanam
lines.translation_en: Who have reached the summit of the universe

lines.transliteration: Namo Saya Savva-Siddhanam
lines.translation_en: I pay homage always to all the Siddhas

lines.transliteration: Jo Devana Vi Devo
lines.translation_en: He who is the god of gods

lines.transliteration: Jam Deva Panjali Namamsanti
lines.translation_en: To whom gods bow with folded hands

lines.transliteration: Tam Deva-Deva-Mahiam
lines.translation_en: That great Lord among gods

lines.transliteration: Sirasa Vande Mahaviram
lines.translation_en: I bow my head to Lord Mahavira

lines.transliteration: Ikko Vi Namukkaro
lines.translation_en: Even one salutation

lines.transliteration: Jinavara-Vasahassa Vaddhamanassa
lines.translation_en: To the supreme Jina, Vardhaman Mahavira

lines.transliteration: Sansara-Sagarao
lines.translation_en: Across the ocean of worldly existence

lines.transliteration: Tarei Naram Va Narim Va
lines.translation_en: Carries a man or a woman across

lines.transliteration: Ujjinta-Sela-Sihare
lines.translation_en: On the summit of Mount Girnar

lines.transliteration: Dikkha Nanam Nisihia Jassa
lines.translation_en: Where He received initiation and perfect knowledge

lines.transliteration: Tam Dhamma-Chakka-Vattim
lines.translation_en: That monarch who turned the wheel of dharma

lines.transliteration: Arittha-Nemim Namamsami
lines.translation_en: I bow to Arishtanemi (Lord Neminath)

lines.transliteration: Cattari Attha Dasa Do Ya
lines.translation_en: Four, eight, ten and two (twenty-four)

lines.transliteration: Vandiya Jinavara Cauvvisam
lines.translation_en: I salute all twenty-four supreme Jinas

lines.transliteration: Paramattha-Nitthi-Attha
lines.translation_en: Who have attained the supreme state of liberation

lines.transliteration: Siddha Siddhim Mama Disantu
lines.translation_en: May the Siddhas grant me salvation

interpretation: This sutra is a prayer to all enlightened Siddhas, Lord Mahavira, Lord Neminath and all twenty-four Tirthankaras installed at Ashtapada Tirtha. It declares that even a single perfect salutation to Lord Mahavira is powerful enough to carry any soul across the ocean of worldly existence — emphasizing the immeasurable merit of sincere devotion.

title: Shree Veyavachcha–Garanam Sootra

lines.transliteration: Veyävachcha-garänam, santi-garänam, Sammadditthi-samähi-garänam karemi käussaggam.
lines.translation_en: I stand in meditation (käyotsarga) for those patron Gods who render selfless service, bring tranquility, and bring calmness to people of right faith.

interpretation: This sutra is recited for the peace of society, in commemoration of the patron gods who look after the Jain religion and society at large, and who bring stability to those with right faith.

title: Shree Bhagavanaham Sootra

lines.transliteration: Bhagavänham, ächäryaham, upädhyäyaham, sarva-sädhuham.
lines.translation_en: Salutation to the Arihantas (Bhagaväns), to the Ächäryas, to the Upädhyäyas, and to all Sädhus and Sädhvis.

interpretation: In this verse, salutation is offered in sequence to the five supreme beings — the Arihantas, Ächäryas, Upädhyäyas, and all Sädhus and Sädhvis — by uttering each phrase along with the Khamasamana sutra.

title: Shree Savvassavi Sootra

lines.transliteration: Ichchhä-kärena sandisaha bhagavan! Devasia padikkamane thäu? Ichchham,
lines.translation_en: O Lord! With your permission, may I repent for the transgressions of the day? I accept your permission.

lines.transliteration: Savvassa vi devasia, duchchintia, dubbhäsia, duchchitthia,
lines.translation_en: For all sinful thoughts, words and activities committed during the day,

lines.transliteration: michchhä mi dukkadam.
lines.translation_en: May those harmful deeds be forgiven and become fruitless.

interpretation: This sutra is recited at the start of Pratikraman to seek permission from the preceptor (or Tirthankar) and to ask forgiveness for all sinful thoughts, words, and actions committed during the day.

title: Shree Ichchhami Thami Sootra

lines.transliteration: Icchami Thami Kaussaggam, Jo Me Devasio
lines.translation_en: I wish to stand in meditation posture for whatever faults I may have committed during the day

lines.transliteration: Aiyaro Kao, Kaio, Vaio, Manasio,
lines.translation_en: Through my deeds, words, and thoughts,

lines.transliteration: Ussutto, Ummaggo, A-Kappo,
lines.translation_en: For speaking against the scriptures, following a wrong path, performing unworthy and improper deeds,

lines.transliteration: A-Karanijjo, Dujjhao, Duvvichintio,
lines.translation_en: For ill-meditated and ill-conceived acts,

lines.transliteration: Anayaro, Avicchiavvo, A-Savaga-Pauggo.
lines.translation_en: For immoral, undesirable, and unbecoming acts for a layman.

lines.transliteration: Nane, Dansane, Charitta-Charitte, Sue, Samaie,
lines.translation_en: In regard to knowledge, belief, conduct of a layman's life, the scriptures, and equanimity (samayika),

lines.transliteration: Tinham Guttinam, Chaunham Kasayanam,
lines.translation_en: Whatever wrong I may have committed in respect to the three-fold restraint vows (guptis) and the four passions (kashayas),

lines.transliteration: Panchanhamanu-Vvayanam, Tinham Guna-Vvayanam,
lines.translation_en: In regard to the five minor vows (anu-vratas) and the three spiritual merit vows (guna-vratas),

lines.transliteration: Chaunham Sikkha-Vayanam, Barasa.
lines.translation_en: In regard to the four spiritual disciplinary vows (shiksha-vratas),

lines.transliteration: Vihassa-Savaga-Dhammassa, Jam Khandiam
lines.translation_en: The layman's twelvefold rule of conduct that I may have broken or opposed — may those bad deeds of mine be forgiven and become fruitless.

lines.transliteration: Jam Virähiam, Tassa Micchämi Dukkadam.
lines.translation_en: For whatever I have transgressed, may those sins be forgiven.

interpretation: This sutra is the formal declaration of intent to perform Kayotsarga specifically for the daily transgressions. The practitioner acknowledges all faults committed during the day — whether subtle or gross — condemns and reproaches them, and surrenders the ego as preparation for the standing meditation.

title: Shree Nanammi Sootra

lines.transliteration: Nänammi dansanammi a, Charanammi tavammi taha ya viriyammi. Äyaranam äyäro, ia eso panchahä bhanio.
lines.translation_en: There are five ethical codes of conduct: right knowledge, right faith, right conduct, right penance, and spiritual strength.

lines.transliteration: Käle vinae bahumäne, uvahäne taha aninhavane. Vanjana-attha-tadubhae, atthaviho nänamäyäro.
lines.translation_en: The eightfold practices of right knowledge are: studying at the proper time, respecting scholars, revering scripture, studying, not speaking ill of the preceptor, correct pronunciation, accurate interpretation, and reflecting on both verses and meaning.

lines.transliteration: Nissankia nikkankhia, nivvitigichchhä amudha-ditthi a. Uvavuha-thirikarane, vachchhalla-pabhävane attha.
lines.translation_en: The eightfold right faith: no doubt, no greed-based faith, no dislike of ascetics' appearance, no awe of miracles, praising right faith, stabilizing others' faith, care for fellow human beings, and glorifying the religion.

lines.transliteration: Panihäna-joga-jutto, panchahim samiihim tihim guttihim. Esa charittäyäro, atthaviho hoi näyavvo.
lines.translation_en: The eightfold right conduct: diligently practicing the fivefold carefulness (samitis) and the threefold restraints (guptis) of mind, speech, and body.

lines.transliteration: Bärasa-vihammi vi tave, sabbhintara-bähire kusala-ditthe. Agiläi anäjivi, näyavvo so taväyäro.
lines.translation_en: The twelve forms of austerity — six external and six internal — as prescribed by the Tirthankar, should be practiced without remorse and without any expectation of reward.

lines.transliteration: Anasana-munoariyä, vitti-sankhevanam rasachchäo. Käya-kileso sanlinayä y bajjho tavo hoi.
lines.translation_en: The six external austerities are: fasting, eating less than required, restricting food items, abstaining from tasty foods, tolerating physical pain, and being modest.

lines.transliteration: Päyachchhittam vinao, veyävachcham taheva sajjhäo. Jhänam ussaggo vi a, abbhintarao tavo hoi.
lines.translation_en: The six internal austerities are: repentance, humility, selfless service, study of scriptures, meditation, and non-attachment to the body.

lines.transliteration: Aniguhia-bala-virio, parakkamai jo jahuttamäutto. Junjai a jahäthämam, näyavvo viriyäyäro.
lines.translation_en: To use mental, verbal, and bodily strength according to one's ability to observe the codes of right knowledge, right faith, right conduct, and right penance — this is the code of spiritual strength.

interpretation: This sutra (also known as Panchächära Ke Atichära) describes in eight verses the five ethical codes of conduct: right knowledge, right faith, right conduct, right penance, and spiritual strength, along with their respective eight-fold sub-practices. It is recited as part of asking forgiveness for any violations of these five codes.

title: Shree Suguru Vandana Sootra

lines.transliteration: Ichchhämi khamä-samano!
lines.translation_en: O monk, I wish (to pay obeisance to you).

lines.transliteration: Vandium jävanijjäe, nisihiäe,
lines.translation_en: To bow to you as is proper, with humility,

lines.transliteration: Anujänaha me miuggaham, nisihi,
lines.translation_en: Please grant me permission to approach you gently. I withdraw from all worldly activities.

lines.transliteration: Aho-käyam käya-samphäsam-khamanijjo bhe! Kilämo?
lines.translation_en: O revered one! May we bear the bodily touch and fatigue of the day? Are you tired?

lines.transliteration: Appa-kilantänam bahu-subhena bhe! Divaso vaikkanto?
lines.translation_en: O revered one! For those who are not tired, has the day passed with much merit and goodness?

lines.transliteration: Jattä bhe? Javanijjam cha bhe? Khämemi khamä-samano!
lines.translation_en: O revered one! How is your health? Is everything proper? O monk, I ask for your forgiveness.

lines.transliteration: Devasiam vaikkamam, ävassiäe padikkamämi,
lines.translation_en: I repent for the transgressions of the day, as it is necessary and obligatory.

lines.transliteration: Khamäsamanänam, devasiäe äsäyanäe tittisannavaräe
lines.translation_en: O monks, for the disrespect shown during the day, in all three types of conduct,

lines.transliteration: Jam kinchi michchhäe, mana-dukkadäe, vaya-dukkadäe,
lines.translation_en: Whatever wrong I have done through false belief, improper thought, or improper speech,

lines.transliteration: Käya-dukkadäe, kohäe, mänäe, mäyäe, lobhäe,
lines.translation_en: Through improper bodily action, anger, pride, deceit, or greed,

lines.transliteration: Savva-käliäe, savva-michchho-vayäräe, Savva-dhammä-ikkamanäe
lines.translation_en: At all times, through all false conduct, and through transgression of all religious duties,

lines.transliteration: äsäyanäe Jo me aiyäro kao, tassa khamä-samano!
lines.translation_en: For whatever transgressions I have committed through disrespect — O monk, I seek your forgiveness.

lines.transliteration: Padikkamämi, nindämi, garihämi, appänam vosirämi.
lines.translation_en: I repent, I censure myself, I reproach myself, and I shed all those sinful acts from my soul.

interpretation: The Suguru Vandana Sutra is a devotional prayer of obeisance to the true Guru (Suguru). The practitioner commits to following the Siddha path without transgression by thought, word or body, and prays for auspiciousness and enlightenment in this very lifetime. It reinforces the centrality of the Guru-disciple relationship in spiritual progress.

title: Shree Devasiam Aloum Sootra

lines.transliteration: Ichchhäkärena sandisaha bhagwan!
lines.translation_en: With your willing permission, O Lord!

lines.transliteration: Devasiam äloum?
lines.translation_en: May I review and confess the faults committed during the day?

lines.transliteration: Ichchham, äloemi,
lines.translation_en: As you wish — I now confess.

lines.transliteration: Jo me devasio.
lines.translation_en: Whatever transgression of mine occurred during the day...

interpretation: This sutra formally initiates the Alochana (reflective confession) portion of the evening Pratikraman. The devotee asks permission from the Lord to review and confess all the day's transgressions, establishing the introspective and soul-cleansing nature of the rite. It marks the transition from ritualistic recitation to deep personal self-examination.

title: Shree Sat Lakha Sootra

lines.transliteration: Säta läkha pruthvikäya, säta läkha apkäya,
lines.translation_en: 7 lakh earth-bodied lives (dirt, stones, etc.), 7 lakh water-bodied lives (water, dew, ice, etc.),

lines.transliteration: Säta läkha teukäya, säta läkha vaukäya,
lines.translation_en: 7 lakh fire-bodied lives (light, fire, candle, torch, etc.), 7 lakh wind-bodied lives (air, fine particles, etc.),

lines.transliteration: Dash läkha pratyeka vanaspatikäya, chauda läkha sädharana vanaspatikäya,
lines.translation_en: 10 lakh individual plant lives (fruits, flowers, seeds, leaves, roots, etc.), 14 lakh collective plant lives (one body holding many lives, such as figs and fig-like fruits, etc.),

lines.transliteration: Be läkha beindriya, be läkha teindriya,
lines.translation_en: 2 lakh two-sensed lives (sea-shells, etc.), 2 lakh three-sensed lives (ants, termites, etc.),

lines.transliteration: Be läkha chaurindriya, chära läkha devata,
lines.translation_en: 2 lakh four-sensed lives (mosquitoes, spiders, etc.), 4 lakh celestial (deva) lives,

lines.transliteration: Chära läkha näraki, chära läkha tiryancha panchendriya, chauda läkha manushya.
lines.translation_en: 4 lakh infernal (näraki) lives, 4 lakh five-sensed animal lives, 14 lakh human lives.

lines.transliteration: Evamkäre chauräshi läkha jiva yoni mähi, mähre jive je koi jiva hanyo hoi, hanävyo hoi, hantän pratye anumodhyo hoi, te savi hun mane, vachane käyae kari, michchhämi dukkadam.
lines.translation_en: Of these 84 lakh (8.4 million) life-forms, whatever living being I have hurt or killed, caused to be hurt, or approved of hurting — mentally, verbally or physically — may all those sinful deeds be forgiven and become fruitless.

interpretation: This sutra enumerates the 84 lakh (8.4 million) yonis — the total categories of birth-forms across all the three worlds — beginning with the one-sensed earth, water, fire, wind and plant bodies, through the two-, three-, and four-sensed beings, and the five-sensed celestial, infernal, animal and human lives. Having recalled the vastness of life, the practitioner seeks forgiveness from every creature they may have harmed or caused to be harmed — by thought, word or deed — embodying the Jain ideal of universal compassion and non-violence.

title: Shree Adhara Papasthanaka Sootra

lines.transliteration: Pahele pränätipäta, bije mrushäväda,
lines.translation_en: First is killing (pränätipäta / himsä), second is lying (mrushäväda),

lines.transliteration: Trije adattädäna, chauthe maithuna,
lines.translation_en: third is stealing (adattädäna), fourth is unchastity (abrahma / maithuna),

lines.transliteration: Pänchame parigraha, chhathe krodha,
lines.translation_en: fifth is acquisitiveness (parigraha), sixth is anger (krodha),

lines.transliteration: Sätme mäna, äthme mäyä,
lines.translation_en: seventh is pride (mäna), eighth is deceit (mäyä),

lines.transliteration: Navme lobha, dashme räga,
lines.translation_en: ninth is greed (lobha), tenth is attachment (räga),

lines.transliteration: Agyärme dwesha, bärme kalaha,
lines.translation_en: eleventh is hatred (dwesha), twelfth is disputation (kalaha),

lines.transliteration: Terame abhyäkhyäna, chaudame paishunya,
lines.translation_en: thirteenth is false accusation (abhyäkhyäna), fourteenth is backbiting (paishunya),

lines.transliteration: Panderame rati-arati, solame para-pariväda,
lines.translation_en: fifteenth is pleasure-displeasure (rati-arati), sixteenth is slander (para-pariväda / nindä),

lines.transliteration: Saterame mäyä mrushäväda, adhärame mithyätva shalya;
lines.translation_en: seventeenth is deceitful speech (mäyä-mrushäväda), and eighteenth is false belief — belief in the wrong god, teacher and religion (mithyätva).

lines.transliteration: Ae adhära, päpasthänakamähen, mähre jive, je koi papa sevayun hoi, sevrävyun hoi, sevatän pratye anumodhyu hoi, te savi hun mane, vachane käyae kari, michchhämi dukkadam.
lines.translation_en: If I have indulged in, promoted or encouraged any such sinful act by others, or praised one who has committed any of these eighteen categories of sin — mentally, verbally or physically — may all those sinful deeds be forgiven and become fruitless.

interpretation: This sutra enumerates the eighteen sinful activities (päpasthänaka) by which evil karmas are accumulated — beginning with the five great transgressions (killing, lying, stealing, unchastity, acquisitiveness), through the four passions (anger, pride, deceit, greed), and continuing through attachment, hatred, disputation, false accusation, backbiting, pleasure-displeasure, slander, deceitful speech, and finally false belief (mithyätva). Having recalled them in order, the practitioner confesses and seeks forgiveness for any of these sins committed, caused, or approved — by thought, word or deed.

title: Shree Ichchhami Padikkamium Sootra

lines.transliteration: Ichchhami Padikkamium
lines.translation_en: I wish to repent.

lines.transliteration: Jo Me Devasio Aiyaro Kao
lines.translation_en: From this sutra, we confess the sin.

interpretation: This sutra is recited to seek the preceptor's permission to formally begin Pratikraman and to ask forgiveness for all the wrong thoughts, words and deeds accumulated during the day (or, in Samvatsari Pratikraman, the year). It marks the transition into the penitential retreat.

title: Shree Vandittu Sootra

lines.transliteration: Vandittu savva-siddhe, dhammäyarie a savva-sähu a; ichchhämi padikkamium, sävaga-dhammäiärassa.
lines.translation_en: Bowing to all the Siddhas, the Dharmacharyas and all the Sadhus, I wish to confess for the transgressions committed while following the layman's vows.

lines.transliteration: Jo me vayäiyäro, näne taha dansane charitte a; suhumo va bäyaro vä, tam ninde tam cha garihämi.
lines.translation_en: Whatever subtle or gross transgression I have committed in respect of right knowledge, right faith and right conduct (and austerity and energy) — I condemn it and reproach it.

lines.transliteration: Duvihe pariggahammi, sävajje bahuvihe a ärambhe; kärävane a karane, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: For the two kinds of possession and for manifold sinful, harmful activities — whether done by me or caused to be done — I confess all the day's faults.

lines.transliteration: Jam baddhamindiehim, chauhim kasäehim appasatthehim; rägena va dosena va, tam ninde tam cha garihämi.
lines.translation_en: Whatever I have bound through the five senses and the four base passions, through attachment or aversion — I condemn it and reproach it.

lines.transliteration: Ägamane-niggamane, thäne chankamane anäbhoge; abhioge a nioge, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: For coming, going, standing, strolling, carelessness, and acting under compulsion or pressure — I confess all the day's faults.

lines.transliteration: Sankä kankha vigichchhä, pasansa taha santhavo kulingisu; sammattassa-iäre, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: For doubt, longing for other faiths, uncertainty, praise of or acquaintance with believers in false doctrines — transgressions of right faith — I confess them all.

lines.transliteration: Chhakkäya-samärambhe, payane a payävane a je dosä; attatthä ya paratthä, ubhayatthä cheva tam ninde.
lines.translation_en: For the harm caused to the six classes of living beings in cooking, causing to cook, or approving it — for myself, for others, or for both — I reproach myself.

lines.transliteration: Panchanhamanu-vvayänam, guna-vvayänam cha tinhamaiyäre; sikkhänam cha chaunham, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: For lapses regarding the five lesser vows (anuvrata), the three merit vows (gunavrata) and the four disciplinary vows (shikshavrata) — I confess all the day's faults.

lines.transliteration: Padhame anu-vvayammi, thulaga-pänäiväya-viraio; äyaria-mappasatthe, ittha pamäya-ppasangenam.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the first vow of non-violence, for what I committed through carelessness or contempt toward living beings —

lines.transliteration: Vaha-bandha-chhavi-chchhee, aibhäre bhatta-päna-vuchchhee; padhama-vayassa-iyäre, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: — such as beating, binding, mutilating, overloading and withholding food and drink — I confess all transgressions of the first vow.

lines.transliteration: Bie anu-vvayammi, parithulaga-aliya-vayana-viraio; äyaria-mappasatthe, ittha pamäya-ppasangenam.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the second vow of truthfulness, for what I committed through carelessness or contempt —

lines.transliteration: Sahasä rahassa däre, mosuvaese a kudalehe a; biya-vayassa-iäre, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: — such as hasty or secret false accusation, false counsel and forging documents — I confess all transgressions of the second vow.

lines.transliteration: Taie anu-vvayammi, thulaga-paradavva-harana-viraio; äyaria-mappasatthe, ittha pamäya-ppasangenam.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the third vow of non-stealing, for what I committed through carelessness or contempt —

lines.transliteration: Tenähada-ppaoge, tappadiruve viruddha-gamane a; kuda-tula kuda-mäne, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: — such as receiving stolen goods, abetting theft, illicit trade, and false weights and measures — I confess all transgressions of the third vow.

lines.transliteration: Chautthe anu-vvayammi, nichcham paradära-gamana-viraio; äyaria-mappasatthe, ittha pamäya-ppasangenam.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the fourth vow of celibacy, for what I committed through carelessness or contempt —

lines.transliteration: Apariggahiä-ittara, ananga-viväha-tivva-anuräge; chauttha-vayassa-iäre, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: — such as relations with unmarried or kept women, unnatural conduct, arranging others' marriages, and intense craving — I confess all transgressions of the fourth vow.

lines.transliteration: Itto anu-vvae panchamammi, äyaria-mappasatthammi; parimäna-parichchhee, ittha pamäya-ppasangenam.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the fifth vow of non-possession, for what I committed through carelessness or contempt in exceeding the set limits —

lines.transliteration: Dhana-dhanna-khitta-vatthu, ruppa-suvanne a kuvia-parimäne; dupae chauppayammi ya, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: — of wealth and grain, land and property, silver and gold, other goods, and two-legged and four-legged beings — I confess all the day's faults.

lines.transliteration: Gamanassa u parimäne, disäsu uddham ahe a tiriam cha; vuddhi sai-antaraddhä, padhamammi guna-vvae ninde.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the first merit vow (limiting directions), I reproach myself for exceeding or forgetting the limits set on movement upward, downward and across.

lines.transliteration: Majjammi a mansammi a, pupphe a phale a gandha-malle a; uvabhoga-paribhoge, biammi guna-vvae ninde.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the second merit vow (limiting enjoyments), I reproach myself for lapses in consumables and reusables — liquor, meat, flowers, fruit, scent and garlands.

lines.transliteration: Sachitte padibaddhe, apoli-duppoliam cha ähäre; tuchchhosahi-bhakkhanayä, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: I confess the day's faults in using sentient things, and eating uncooked, half-cooked, or worthless food.

lines.transliteration: Ingäli-vana-sädi-, bhädi-phodi suvajjae kammam; vänijjam cheva danta-lakkha-rasa-kesa-visa-visayam.
lines.translation_en: A layperson should strictly avoid the harmful occupations — trades in fire and charcoal, forest-clearing, carts, hire, and quarrying, and commerce in ivory, lac, liquor, hair and poison.

lines.transliteration: Evam khu janta-pillana kammam, nillanchhanam cha dava-dänam; sara-daha-taläya-sosam, asai-posam cha vajjijjä.
lines.translation_en: Likewise one should avoid operating mills and presses, mutilating animals, setting fires, draining lakes and reservoirs, and rearing creatures for immoral gain.

lines.transliteration: Satthaggi-musala-jantaga-tana-katthe manta-mula-bhesajje; dinne davävie vä, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: I confess the day's faults in giving, or causing to be given, weapons, fire-furnaces, pestles, mills, straw, wood, spells, roots or potions.

lines.transliteration: Nhänu-vvattana-vannaga-vilevane sadda-ruva-rasa-gandhe; vatthäsana-äbharane, padikkame desiam savvam.
lines.translation_en: I confess the day's faults in excessive bathing, anointing and cosmetics, indulging the senses in sound, form, taste and scent, and in clothes, seats and ornaments.

lines.transliteration: Kandappe kukkuie, mohari-ahigarana-bhoga-airitte; dandammi anatthäe, taiammi-guna-vvae ninde.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the third merit vow (purposeless harm), I reproach myself for vulgar speech, crude jest, idle chatter, keeping harmful instruments, and excessive indulgence.

lines.transliteration: Tivihe duppanihäne, ana-vatthäne tahä sai-vihune; sämäiya-vitaha-kae, padhame sikkhä-vae ninde.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the first disciplinary vow (samayika), I reproach myself for misconduct of mind, speech and body, instability, forgetfulness, and improper performance.

lines.transliteration: Änavane pesavane, sadde ruve a puggala-kkheve; desävagäsiammi, bie sikkhä-vae ninde.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the second disciplinary vow (deshavakashika), I reproach myself for sending or fetching beyond the set limits, and signaling by sound, sight or throwing objects.

lines.transliteration: Santhäruchchära-vihi-pamäya taha cheva bhoyanä-bhoe; posaha-vihi-vivarie, taie sikkhä-vae ninde.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the third disciplinary vow (paushadha), I reproach myself for carelessness in spreading the mat and in bodily functions, and for negligence about food.

lines.transliteration: Sachitte nikkhivane, pihine vavaesa-machchhare cheva; käläikkama-däne, chautthe sikkhä-vae ninde.
lines.translation_en: Regarding the fourth disciplinary vow (sharing with guests), I reproach myself for covering alms with sentient things, false pretexts, jealousy, and giving after the proper time.

lines.transliteration: Suhiesu a duhiesu a, jä me assanjaesu anukampä; rägena va dosena va, tam ninde tam cha garihämi.
lines.translation_en: For the compassion or aversion I showed — out of attachment or hatred — toward the unrestrained, whether happy or suffering, I condemn it and reproach it.

lines.transliteration: Sähusu samvibhägo, na kao tava-charana-karana-juttesu; sante phäsua-däne, tam ninde tam cha garihämi.
lines.translation_en: For failing to share with monks endowed with austerity and conduct when pure, blameless alms were available, I condemn it and reproach it.

lines.transliteration: Iha-loe para-loe, jivia-marane a äsansa-paoge; pancha-viho aiäro, mä majjha hujja maranante.
lines.translation_en: May I not commit, at the time of death, any of the five transgressions of the vow of holy death — desire for this world or the next, for life or death, or for sensual reward.

lines.transliteration: Käena käiassa, padikkame väiassa väyäe; manasä mänasiassa, savvassa vayäiärassa.
lines.translation_en: By body for bodily faults, by speech for verbal faults, by mind for mental faults — I confess every transgression of the vows.

lines.transliteration: Vandana-vaya-sikkhä-gäravesu, sannä-kasäya-dandesu; guttisu a samiisu a, jo aiäro a tam ninde.
lines.translation_en: For any transgression regarding worship, vows and learning, the three prides, the instincts and passions, the three evil activities, the threefold restraint and fivefold vigilance — I condemn it.

lines.transliteration: Sammaddatthi jivo, jai vi hu pävam samäyarai kinchi; appo si hoi bandho, jena na niddhandhasam kunai.
lines.translation_en: A soul of right faith, even if it commits some sin, incurs only a slight karmic bond, because it does not act with ruthlessness.

lines.transliteration: Tam pi hu sapadikkamanam, sappariävam sauttara-gunam cha; khippam uvasämei, vähi vva susikkhio vijjo.
lines.translation_en: And that bond too, accompanied by repentance and atonement, it quickly subdues — as a well-trained physician cures disease.

lines.transliteration: Jahä visam kuttha-gayam, manta-mula-visärayä; vijjä hananti mantehim, to tam havai nivvisam.
lines.translation_en: Just as experts in spells and herbs render the poison spread in a body harmless by their mantras —

lines.transliteration: Evam attha-viham kammam, räga-dosa-samajjiam; äloanto a nindanto, khippam hanai susävao.
lines.translation_en: — so a good layperson, confessing and condemning, swiftly destroys the eightfold karma accumulated through attachment and aversion.

lines.transliteration: Kaya-pävo vi manusso, äloia nindia guru-sagäse; hoi airega-lahuo, oharia-bharuvva bhäravaho.
lines.translation_en: Even one who has done evil, confessing and condemning before the guru, becomes exceedingly light — like a porter who has set down his burden.

lines.transliteration: Ävassaena eena, sävao jaivi bahurao hoi; dukkhänamanta-kiriam, kähi achirena kälena.
lines.translation_en: By this essential rite (avashyaka), a layperson, though laden with karma, will in a short time bring an end to suffering.

lines.transliteration: Äloanä bahuvihä, na ya sambhariä padikkamana-käle; mula-guna-uttara-gune, tam ninde tam cha garihämi.
lines.translation_en: For the manifold lapses regarding the principal and secondary vows not recalled at the time of Pratikraman, I condemn them and reproach them.

lines.transliteration: Tassa dhammassa kevali-pannattassa, abbhutthio mi ärähanäe, virao mi virähanäe; tivihena padikkanto, vandämi jine chauvvisam.
lines.translation_en: Risen to the practice of the dharma taught by the Omniscient and withdrawn from its violation, having confessed in three ways, I bow to the twenty-four Jinas.

lines.transliteration: Jävanti cheiäim, uddhe a ahe a tiria-loe a; savväim täim vande, iha santo tattha santäim.
lines.translation_en: To all the temple-images in the upper, lower and middle worlds — present here in spirit, I salute all of them there.

lines.transliteration: Jävanta ke vi sähu, bharaheravaya-mahävidehe a; savvesim tesim panao, tivihena tidanda-virayänam.
lines.translation_en: To all the monks in Bharata, Airavata and Mahavideha, restrained from the three rods — I bow to all of them in three ways.

lines.transliteration: Chira-sanchiya-päva-panäsanii, bhava-saya-sahassa-mahanie; chauvisa-jina-viniggaya-kahäi, volantu me diahä.
lines.translation_en: May my days pass amid the discourse of the twenty-four Jinas, which destroys long-accumulated sin and ends hundreds of thousands of births.

lines.transliteration: Mama mangala-marihantä, siddhä sähu suam cha dhammo a; samma-dditthi devä, dintu samähim cha bohim cha.
lines.translation_en: May the Arihants, Siddhas, Sadhus, the scripture and the dharma be auspicious to me; may the right-faithful gods grant me equanimity and enlightenment.

lines.transliteration: Padisiddhänam karane, kichchäna-makarane padikkamanam; asaddahane a tahä, vivariä-paruvanäe a.
lines.translation_en: Pratikraman is performed for doing the forbidden, leaving the prescribed undone, disbelief, and contrary preaching.

lines.transliteration: Khämemi savva-jive, savve jivä khamantu me; mitti me savva-bhuesu, veram majjha na kenai.
lines.translation_en: I forgive all living beings; may all living beings forgive me. I have friendship with all beings and enmity with none.

lines.transliteration: Evamaham äloia, nindia-garahia-duganchhiam sammam; tivihena padikkanto, vandämi jine chauvvisam.
lines.translation_en: Thus, having confessed, condemned, reproached and despised my faults rightly, withdrawn in three ways, I bow to the twenty-four Jinas.

interpretation: This is the longest principal aphorism of both the evening (Devasika) and morning (Rai) Pratikraman. After bowing to the Siddhas, Dharmacharyas and Sadhus, the layperson walks systematically through the five codes of conduct and the twelve householder vows — the five Anuvratas, three Gunavratas and four Shikshavratas — confessing each way they may have faltered, then affirms that sincere confession before the guru swiftly destroys karma, and closes with universal forgiveness and obeisance to the twenty-four Jinas.

title: Shree Ayariya Uvajzae Sootra

lines.transliteration: Äyariya-uvajjhäe, sise sähammie kula-gane a. Je me kei kasäyä, savve tivihena khämemi.
lines.translation_en: O Acharya, Upadhyaya, co-disciples, members of my Kula (group) and Gana (larger group)! For whatever passions I may have expressed towards any of you, I ask forgiveness in three ways (mind, speech, body).

lines.transliteration: Savvassa samana-sanghassa, bhagavao anjalim karia sise. Savvam khamävaittä, khamämi savvassa ahayam pi.
lines.translation_en: To the entire monastic order, I bow with folded hands. Having sought forgiveness from all, I forgive all from the bottom of my heart.

lines.transliteration: Savvassa jiva-räsissa, bhävao dhamma-nihia-nia-chitto. Savvam khamävaittä, khamämi savvassa ahayam pi.
lines.translation_en: To all the multitudes of souls, with a mind established in righteous feelings, having sought forgiveness from all, I forgive all from the bottom of my heart.

interpretation: This sutra is the most expansive declaration of universal forgiveness in Pratikraman. The practitioner asks forgiveness from all five types of spiritual leaders and every living being, while simultaneously granting forgiveness to all. It embodies the Jain ideal of universal friendship (Maitri) and absence of enmity, culminating in the supreme prayer of Michchhami Dukkadam.

title: Shree Shrutadevata Stuti

lines.transliteration: Sua-devayä bhagavai, nänä-varaniya-kamma-sanghäyam. Tesim khaveu sayayam, jesim sua-säyare bhatti.
lines.translation_en: O blessed Goddess of Learning! Please always destroy the multitude of various knowledge-obscuring karmas of those who have devotion in the ocean of scriptures.

interpretation: This thoy (short stuti) offers praise to Shrutdevta — the goddess of sacred knowledge and learning who presides over the Jain scriptures (Shruta). In the Jain tradition, Saraswati Devi is honored as the guardian of scriptural wisdom, and this prayer seeks her blessings for the preservation and understanding of Jain Agamas.

title: Shree Kshetradevata Stuti

lines.transliteration: Yasyäh ksetram samäsritya, sädhubhih sädhyate kriyä. Sä ksetra-devatä nityam, bhuyännah sukha-däyini.
lines.translation_en: May that Goddess of the Field (Ksetra Devata), in whose territory the monks perform religious rituals, always be a source of happiness for us.

interpretation: This thoy offers praise to the Kshetra Devta — the protecting deity of the sacred place or pilgrimage site (Tirth Kshetra). In Jain tradition, each temple and pilgrimage site has a guardian deity who safeguards the holy ground. This prayer honors that divine protector and seeks continued protection of the sacred space.

title: Shree Kamaladala Stuti

lines.transliteration: Kamala-dala-vipula-nayanä, Kamala-mukhi kamala-garbha-sama-gauri. Kamale sthitä bhagavati, Dadätu sruta-devatä siddhim.
lines.translation_en: The Goddess of Learning (Sruta Devata), with eyes large as lotus petals, lotus face, complexion as fair as the interior of a lotus, seated on a lotus — may she grant us spiritual accomplishment.

interpretation: This thoy (short praise) invokes the imagery of the Lord's eyes being as wide and pure as lotus petals — a classical devotional metaphor in Jain literature. It glorifies the Tirthankara as the eternal propagator of the Jain Shashan (teachings), connecting physical beauty with spiritual radiance.

title: Shree Bhavana-Devata Stuti

lines.transliteration: Jnänädi-guna-yutänäm, nityam svädhyäya-sanyama-ratänäm. Vidadhätu bhavana-devi, sivam sadä sarva-sädhunäm.
lines.translation_en: May the Goddess of Dwelling (Bhavana Devi) always bestow auspiciousness on all the monks who are endowed with virtues like right knowledge and are always devoted to self-study and self-restraint.

interpretation: This thoy offers praise to the Bhuvana Devta — the presiding deity of the Samavasarana (the divine assembly hall of the Tirthankara). In Jain cosmology, each Samavasarana has a guardian deity who maintains order and sanctity in the Lord's assembly. This prayer honors that divine presence.

title: Shree Kshetradevata Stuti (Jise Khitte)

lines.transliteration: Jise khitte sähü, dansana-nänehi carana-sahiehi. Sähanti mukkha-maggam, sä devi harau duriäim.
lines.translation_en: The goddess of the region may ward off all obstacles, in the area where the Sädhus are striving on the path of salvation through right faith, right knowledge, and right conduct.

interpretation: Only men recite this Stuti during Pratikraman. By praying to the goddess of the region, we request her to remove any obstacles that may occur during religious activity.

title: Shree Namoastu Vardhamanaya Sootra

lines.transliteration: Namostu varddhamänäya, Sparddhamänäya karmanä. Tajjayä-väpta-moksäya, Paroksäya kutirthinäm.
lines.translation_en: Salutation to Lord Vardhamana (Mahavira), who struggled against and conquered his karmas, attained liberation through that victory, and remains beyond the reach of believers in false faiths.

lines.transliteration: Yesäm vikachä-ravinda-räjyä, Jyäyah krama-kamalä-valim dadhatyä. Sadrsairiti sangatam prasasyam, Kathitam santu siväya te jinendräh.
lines.translation_en: May those Jinendras be auspicious to us, whose lotus-soft feet, as they walk, rest upon rows of golden lotuses fashioned by the gods — of which it is fittingly said, 'such likeness is praiseworthy.'

lines.transliteration: Kasäya-täpä-rdita-jantu-nirvrtim, Karoti yo jaina-mukhämbudod-gatah. Sa sukra-mäsodbhava-vrsti-sannibho, Dadhätu tustim mayi vistaro giräm.
lines.translation_en: May the abundant stream of Jain speech, issuing from the Jina's mouth and bringing peace to beings scorched by the passions — like the first heavy rain at the onset of the monsoon — grant me contentment.

interpretation: This three-verse Sanskrit stuti, recited during the evening Pratikraman, offers salutation to Lord Vardhamana Mahavira — who conquered his karmas and won liberation — then to all the Jinendras, upon whose feet the gods fashion golden lotuses, and finally to the Jinavani (the Jina's teaching), whose words bring peace to beings afflicted by the passions like the first monsoon rain.

title: Shree Vishala Lochana Sootra

lines.transliteration: Visäla-lochana-dalam, prodyad-dantänsu-kesaram. Prätar-vira-jinendrasya, mukha-padmam punätu vah.
lines.translation_en: May the lotus-like morning face of Vira Jinendra (Mahavira), with large eyes for petals and gleaming teeth for filaments, purify you.

lines.transliteration: Yesämabhiseka-karma krtvä, Mattä harsa-bharät sukham surendräh. Trnamapi ganayanti naiva näkam, Prätah santu siväya te jinendräh.
lines.translation_en: May those Jinendras be auspicious for us in the morning — at whose consecration ceremony, the proud and joyful Indras counted not even heaven as a straw (i.e., considered it worthless).

lines.transliteration: Kalanka-nirmukta-mamukta-purnatam, Kutarka-rähu-grasanam sadodayam. Apurva-chandram jina-chandra-bhäsitam, Dinä-game naumi budhair-namaskrtam.
lines.translation_en: I bow in the morning to the unique moon of Jina-knowledge — free from the blemish of ignorance, fully risen, beyond being eclipsed by Rahu of false logic, always risen, and saluted by the wise.

interpretation: This stotra describes the divine physical attributes and spiritual qualities of the Jina — the wide lotus-like eyes, serene countenance, perfect peace and complete detachment. It is a meditative visualization of the Lord's murti (form), designed to inspire deep devotion and inner tranquility in the practitioner during Pratikraman.

title: Shree Addhaijjesu Sootra

lines.transliteration: Addhäijjesu diva-samuddesu, Panarasasu kamma-bhumisu; Jävanta ke vi sähu, Raya-harana-guchchha-padiggaha-dharä.
lines.translation_en: In the two and a half continents and the fifteen karma-bhumis (lands of action), all the monks who carry the broom, cluster (guchchha), and begging bowl (padiggaha)—

lines.transliteration: Pancha-maha-vvaya-dharä, Atthärasa-sahassa-silanga-dharä; Akkhuyä-yära-carittä, Te savve sirasä manasä, matthaena vandämi.
lines.translation_en: —who observe the five great vows, who observe the 18,000 aspects of conduct, whose conduct is unimpaired — I bow to all of them with head, mind, and forehead.

interpretation: This sutra offers obeisance to the Ganadhars — the chief disciples who received the teachings directly from the Tirthankaras and organized them into the Jain Agamas. It extends the salutation to the entire Sangha of monks and nuns, honoring the unbroken chain of spiritual transmission from the Jinas to the present day.

title: Shree Vara-Kanaka

lines.transliteration: Varkanaka shankha vidruma, markata ghan sannibham vigatamoham; saptatishatam jinänäm, sarvämara pujitam vande.
lines.translation_en: I bow to the 170 passionless Pathfinders (Jinas), some of whom have complexions yellow like pure gold, white like a conch-shell, red like coral, green like an emerald, or dark like rain-clouds — worshipped by all the gods.

interpretation: By this single-verse stuti, salutation is offered to the 170 living Tirthankaras (the greatest number present at one time), describing their varied complexions — gold, conch-white, coral-red, emerald-green and cloud-dark. It is traditionally recited by males.

title: Shree Laghu Shanti

lines.transliteration: Shäntim shänti-nishäntam, shäntam shäntä-sivam namaskrtya. Stotuh shänti-nimittam, mantra-padaih shäntaye staumi.
lines.translation_en: Having bowed to the peaceful, the utterly peaceful, the calm and auspicious (Shanti Jinendra), for the peace of the devotee, I praise with the words of mantra for peace.

lines.transliteration: Omiti nischita-vachase, namo namo bhagavaterhate pujäm. Shänti-jinäya jayavate, yasasvine svämine daminäm.
