lines.translation_en: With the word Om (signifying certainty), salutation upon salutation to the blessed Arhat; I offer worship to Shanti Jina, the victorious, the glorious, the master of the self-controlled.

lines.transliteration: Sakalätisesaka-mahä-sampatti-samanvitäya sasyäya. Trailokya-pujitäya cha, namo namah shänti-deväya.
lines.translation_en: Salutation again and again to the God of Peace (Shanti-Deva), endowed with all-surpassing great prosperity, worshipped by the three worlds.

lines.transliteration: Sarvämara-susamuha-svämika-sampujitäya na jitäya. Bhuvana-jana-pälanodyata-tamäya satatam namas-tasmai.
lines.translation_en: Perpetual salutation to him who is worshipped by all the gods and their groups of lords, who is unconquered, and who is ever-intent on protecting the beings of the world.

lines.transliteration: Sarva-duritaugha-näsana-karäya sarväsiva-prasamanäya. Dusta graha-bhuta-pisächa-säkininäm pramathanäya.
lines.translation_en: To him who destroys all floods of sins, who allays all inauspiciousness, who crushes evil planetary influences, ghosts, demons, and sorcerers.

lines.transliteration: Yasyeti näma-mantra-pradhäna-väkyopayoga-krta-tosä. Vijayä kurute jana-hita-miti cha nutä namata tam shäntim.
lines.translation_en: Vijaya (the presiding deity), pleased by the use of the chief mantra sentence of whose (Shanti Jina's) name, brings victory and benefits to people — bow to that Shanti (Lord of Peace).

lines.transliteration: Bhavatu namaste bhagavati! Vijaye! Sujaye! Paräparairajite! Aparäjite! Jagatyäm, jayatiti jayävahe! Bhavati!
lines.translation_en: I salute you O Divine (Bhagavati), Vijayä, Sujaya, Ajita and Aparäjita — all four undefeatable Goddesses, ever-victorious (Jayävaha) and helpful (Bhavati Devi) — as the strength of your mystic spells mysteriously brings triumph upon this world.

lines.transliteration: Sarvasyäpi cha sanghasya, bhadra-kalyäna-mangala-pradade! Sädhunäm cha sadä siva-su-tushti-pushti-prade! Jiyäh.
lines.translation_en: Victory to you, O Goddess! Who bestows welfare, auspiciousness and blessings upon the entire fourfold Jain congregation, and grants mental peace (su-tushti) and prosperity (pushti) to the revered monks.

lines.transliteration: Bhavyänäm krta-siddhe! Nivrti-nirväna-janani! Sattvänäm; Abhaya-pradäna-nirate! Namostu svasti-prade tubhyam.
lines.translation_en: I salute you, O Goddess! Who fulfils the goals of worthy souls (bhavya jivas), the mother of liberation and final release, ever intent on granting fearlessness to all beings — salutation to you, the bestower of well-being.

lines.transliteration: Bhaktänäm jantunäm, subhävahe! Nityam-udyate! Devi! Samyag-drstinäm dhrti rati, mati buddhi pradänäya.
lines.translation_en: O Goddess, ever-active benefactor of devoted beings! You bestow patience, love, understanding and knowledge upon the people of right faith.

lines.transliteration: Jina-säsana-niratänäm, shänti-natänäm cha jagati janatänäm; Shri-sampat-kirti-yaso varddhani! Jaya devi! Vijayasva.
lines.translation_en: O Goddess, devoted to the Jain order and bowing to Lord Shäntinätha — for the people of the world dedicated to the Jain teachings, expand their wealth, glory and fame. Be triumphant, O Goddess; be victorious!

lines.transliteration: Salilänala-visa-visahara, dushta-graha-räja-roga-rana-bhayatah; Räkshasa-ripu-gana-märi, chaureti svä-padädibhyah.
lines.translation_en: From fear of water, fire, poison and snakes; from evil planetary gods, kings, disease and war; from demons, hosts of enemies, plagues, robbers, wild beasts and the like —

lines.transliteration: Atha raksha raksha su-sivam, kuru kuru shäntim cha kuru kuru sadeti; Tushtim kuru kuru pushtim, kuru kuru svastim cha kuru kuru tvam.
lines.translation_en: Protect us, protect us! Bring about auspiciousness, bring peace, always; grant full satisfaction, grant prosperity, and grant well-being upon us.

lines.transliteration: Bhagavati! Guna-vati! Siva-shänti-tushti-pushti-svastiha kuru kuru janänäm; Omiti namo namo hräm hrim hrum hrah, yah kshah hrim phat phat svähä.
lines.translation_en: O Divine and Virtuous Goddess! Bestow welfare, peace, satisfaction, strength and well-being upon the people — Om, namo namo, hräm hrim hrum hrah, yah kshah hrim, phat phat svähä.

lines.transliteration: Evam yan-nämäksara-purah-saram, sanstutä jayä-devi; Kurute shäntim namatäm, namo namah shäntaye tasmai.
lines.translation_en: Thus praised with the syllables of His name, Goddess Jayä brings peace to those who bow. I pay my obeisance again and again to that Lord of Peace.

lines.transliteration: Iti purva-suri-darsita, mantra-pada-vidarbhitah stavah shänteh; Salilädi-bhaya-vinäsi, shäntyädi-karas cha bhakti-matäm.
lines.translation_en: Thus, as revealed by the masters of old, this hymn of praise to Lord Shäntinätha, woven with mystic mantra-words, destroys all fears beginning with water and bestows peace upon the devotees.

lines.transliteration: Yas-chainam pathati sadä, srnoti bhävayati vä yathä-yogam; Sa hi shänti-padam yäyät, surih shri-mänadevas cha.
lines.translation_en: Whoever recites, listens to, or contemplates this hymn each day according to their ability — along with its composer Ächärya Shri Mänadeva Suri — shall swiftly attain the state of eternal peace.

lines.transliteration: Upasargäh ksayam yänti, chhidyante vighna-vallayah; Manah prasannatäm eti, pujyamäne jinesvare.
lines.translation_en: When Lord Jineshvara is worshipped, all calamities are destroyed, the creepers of obstacles are cut away, and the mind attains serene clarity.

lines.transliteration: Sarva-mangala-mängalyam, sarva-kalyäna-käranam; Pradhänam sarva-dharmänäm, jainam jayati säsanam.
lines.translation_en: The most auspicious of all auspicious things, the cause of all welfare, foremost among all religions — victorious is the teaching of the Jina.

interpretation: The Laghu Shanti Stavan (Short Peace Prayer), composed by Ächärya Shri Mänadeva Suri, is one of the most beloved compositions in Jain liturgy. The opening seven verses praise Lord Shäntinätha as the storehouse of peace, while verses 8–15 invoke Vijayä Devi (the Goddess of Victory) for the protection and prosperity of the fourfold Sangha, culminating in the mystic mantra of Shäntinätha's name. The closing verses (16–19) declare the hymn a destroyer of all fears and affirm the eternal victory of the Jain teachings.

title: Shree Chaukkasaya Sootra

lines.transliteration: Chaukkasäya-padimallulluranu, Dujjaya-mayana-bäna-musumuranu. Sarasa-piyangu-vannu gaya-gämiu, Jayau päsu bhuvana-ttaya-sämiu.
lines.translation_en: Lord Pärshvanätha, the master of all three worlds, endowed with golden complexion and with a gait like an elephant, destroyer of all four passions and one who has cut apart Cupid's arrow, may you be ever victorious.

lines.transliteration: Jasu tanu-kanti-kadappa-siniddhau, Sohai phani-mani-kiranä-liddhau. Nam nava-jala-hara-tadillaya-lanchhiu, So jinu päsu payachchhau vanchhiu.
lines.translation_en: O Lord Pärshvanätha, your graceful body shines with rays emitted by the jewel on the hood of the cobra covering your head and by lightning accompanying torrential rain; grant me that which I desire.

interpretation: This hymn in praise of Lord Pärshvanätha is recited while performing Pratikraman. It extols his destruction of the four passions and his supreme mastery over the three worlds.

title: Shree Bharahesara Sajzaya

lines.transliteration: Bharahesara bähubali, abhayakumäro a dhandhanakumäro; sirio annniäutto, aimutto nägadatto a.
lines.translation_en: Emperor Bharat, Bahubali, Abhayakumar, Dhandhankumar, Shriyak (younger brother of Sthulibhadra), Arnikaputra, Atimuktakumar, and Nagdutt.

lines.transliteration: Meajja thulabhaddo, vayararisi nandisena sinhagiri; kayavanno a sukosala, pundario kesi karakandu.
lines.translation_en: Metaraj Muni, Sthulibhadra, Vajra Swami, Nandishen, Sinha Giri, Krutpunya, Sukoshal Muni, Pundarika Muni, Keshi Kumar and Karkundu Muni.

lines.transliteration: Halla vihalla sudansana, säla mahäsäla sälibhaddo a; bhaddo dasannabhaddo, pasannachando a jasabhaddo.
lines.translation_en: Hall Kumar, Vihall Kumar, Sudarshan Sheth, Shal Muni, Maha Shal Muni, Shalibhadra, Bhadrabahu Swami, King Dasharnabhadra, Prasannachandra Muni and Yashobhadrasuri.

lines.transliteration: Jambupahu vankachulo, gayasukumälo avantisukumälo; dhanno iläiputtto, chiläiputto a bähumuni.
lines.translation_en: Jambu Swami, Vankachul, Gajasukumal, Avantisukumal, Dhana Sheth, Illaichiputra, Chilaitiputra and Yuga Bahu Muni.

lines.transliteration: Ajjagiri ajjarakkhia, ajjasuhatthi udäyago manago; kälayasuri sambo, pajjunno muladevo a.
lines.translation_en: Aryamahagiri, Aryarakshitsuri, Aryasuhastisuri, Udayan Rajarshi, Manakputra, Kalikacharya, Shambkumar, Pradyumankumar and King Muldev.

lines.transliteration: Pabhavo vinhukumäro, addakumäro dadhappahäri a; sijjansa kuragadu a, sijjambhava mehakumäro a.
lines.translation_en: Prabhav Swami, Vishnukumar, Ardrakumar, Dadhprahari, Shreyans Kumar, Kurgadu Muni, Shayambhav Acharya and Meghakumar.

lines.transliteration: Emäi mahäsattä, dintu suham guna ganehim sanjuttä; jesim nämaggahane, pävappabandhä vilayam janti.
lines.translation_en: Reciting the names of these and other such extraordinary virtuous persons brings us tranquility and destroys our sins.

lines.transliteration: Sulasä chandanbälä, manoramä mayanarehä damayanti; namayäsundari siyä, nandä bhaddä subhaddä ya.
lines.translation_en: Sulsa, Chandanbala, Manorma, Madanrekha, Damayanti, Narmadasundari, Sita Sati, Nanda, Bhadra Shethani and Subhadra.

lines.transliteration: Räimäi risidattä, paumävai anjanä siridevi; jittha sujittha migävai, pabhävai chillanä devi.
lines.translation_en: Rajimati, Rushidatta, Padmavati, Anjanasundari, Shridevi, Jyeshtha, Sujyeshtha, Mrugavati, Prabhavati and Chelna Rani.

lines.transliteration: Bambhi sundari ruppini, revai kunti sivä jayanti ya; devai dovai dhärani, kalävai pupphachulä ya.
lines.translation_en: Brahmi, Sundari, Rukmani, Revati Shravika, Kunti, Shiva, Jayanti, Devki, Draupadi, Dharini, Kalavati and Puspachula.

lines.transliteration: Paumävai ya gori, gandhäri lakkhamanä susimä ya; jambuvai sachchabhämä, ruppini kanhattha mahisio.
lines.translation_en: Padmavati, Gauri, Gandhari, Lakshmana, Susima, Jambuvati, Satyabhama and Rukmani — all these eight royal queens of Lord Krishna.

lines.transliteration: Jakkhä ya jakkhadinnä, bhuä taha cheva bhuadinnä ya; senä venä renä, bhainio thulbhaddassa.
lines.translation_en: Yaksha, Yakshdatta, Bhuta, Bhutdatta, Sena, Vena and Rena — all these seven sisters of Sthulibhadra.

lines.transliteration: Ichchäi mahäsaio, jayanti akalankasilakaliäo; ajja vi vajjai jäsim, jasa padaho tihuane sayale.
lines.translation_en: All these chaste women, bearers of immaculate disposition and conduct, whose fame is spread over the three worlds even today — may they all be triumphant.

interpretation: This sajjhay (svadhyaya), recited in the morning hours of Rai Pratikraman, eulogizes the extraordinary great souls of the past — 53 virtuous men (gathas 1-6) and 47 virtuous women (gathas 8-13) — who lived ideal Jain lives. Recalling their names and exemplary conduct brings tranquility, inspires similar virtues, and is said to destroy sins.

title: Shree Manahajinanam Sajzaya

lines.transliteration: Mannaha jinänamänam, michchham pariharaha, dharaha sammattam. Chhavviha-ävassayammi, ujjutto hoi pai-divasam.
lines.translation_en: Following the Tirthankars' preachings of Ahimsa, give up wrong beliefs, accept right faith, and diligently perform the six essential duties every day.

lines.transliteration: Pavvesu posaha-vayam, dänam silam tavo a bhävo a. Sajjhäya namukkäro, parovayäro a jayanä a.
lines.translation_en: Observe Paushadhvrata during religious festivals; practice charity, faithfulness to your spouse, austerities, reflection; study scriptures, pay obeisance, help others, and protect living beings.

lines.transliteration: Jina-puä jina-thunanam, guru-thua sähammiäna vacchhallam. Vavahärassa ya suddhi, raha-jattä tittha-jattä ya.
lines.translation_en: Worship Tirthankars, recite their hymns of praise, praise the spiritual preceptor, be affectionate toward fellow human beings, be honest in all business dealings, organize religious seminars, and visit pilgrimage places.

lines.transliteration: Uvasama-vivega-samvara, bhäsä-samii chajiva-karunä ya. Dhammia-jana-samsaggo, karana-damo carana-parinaämo.
lines.translation_en: Be peaceful, have discretion, stop inflow of karma, be watchful of language, have compassion toward all six types of living beings, keep company of spiritual people, control your sense organs, and follow the code of conduct.

lines.transliteration: Samghovari bahu-mäno, putthaya-lihanam pabhävanä titthe. Saddähäna kichchameam, nichcham sugurü-vaesenam.
lines.translation_en: Show great reverence to the Jain congregation, study and copy religious literature, promote religion at pilgrimage places. These are the thirty-six worthy acts for a layperson, to be performed according to the guidance of a true preceptor.

interpretation: This Sajjhäya describes the 36 essential duties recommended for a Jain layperson. The activities help one become righteous, bring equanimity, and attract others to join the congregation. They are to be performed according to one's individual capacity under the guidance of a true spiritual preceptor.

title: Shree Sakala-Teertha Sootra

lines.transliteration: Sakala tirtha vandun kara joda, jinvara näme mangala kroda; pahele svarge läkha batrisha, jinvara chaitya namu nisha disha.
lines.translation_en: With folded hands I worship all the places of pilgrimage, for in the name of the Jina crores of auspicious things arise. In the first heaven there are 32 lakh Jina-temples; I pay my respect daily to all the Jina images in them.

lines.transliteration: Bije läkha atthävisha kahyä, trije bär läkha saddahyä; chothe svarge ada lakha dhära, pänchame vandun läkha ja chära.
lines.translation_en: In the second heaven there are 28 lakh, in the third 12 lakh, in the fourth 8 lakh, and in the fifth 4 lakh temples; I pay homage to all the Jina images in them.

lines.transliteration: Chhatthe svarge sahasa pachäsha, sätme chälisha sahasa präsäda; äthame svarge chha hajära, nava dashame vandun shata chära.
lines.translation_en: In the sixth heaven there are 50,000, in the seventh 40,000 temples; in the eighth 6,000, and in the ninth and tenth 400 each; I pay homage to all the Jina images in them.

lines.transliteration: Agyära bärame tranashe sära, nava graiveyake tranashe adhära; päncha anuttara sarve mali, läkha choräshi adhikän vali.
lines.translation_en: In the eleventh and twelfth heavens there are 300 each, in the nine Graiveyakas 318, and in the five Anuttara heavens 5; in all, there are more than 84 lakh Jain temples.

lines.transliteration: sahasa sattanu trevisa sara, jinavara bhavana tano adhikara; lamba so jojana vistara, pachasa uncha bahotera dhara.
lines.translation_en: There are 97,023 thousand exquisite temples of Tirthankaras. The dimensions of each temple in the upper world are 100 yojanas in length, 50 yojanas wide and 72 yojanas in height. I pay homage to all of them.

lines.transliteration: eka so ensi bimba pramana, sabha sahita eka chaitye jana; so kroda bavana kroda sambhala, lakha choranu sahasa chauala.
lines.translation_en: In each Jina temple with an assembly hall there are 180 images; those without have 120. That makes 1,529,444,760 images in total. I bow to all of them.

lines.transliteration: satase upara satha visala, savi bimba pranamu trana kala; sata kroda ne bahotera lakha, bhavanapatima deva bhakha.
lines.translation_en: In the abyss of the middle world, where there are residences for Bhavanapatis (palace-dwelling celestial beings), there are 77,200,000 huge temples. I bow to all the images therein.

lines.transliteration: eka so ensi bimba pramana, eka eka chaitye sankhya jana; terase kroda nevyasi kroda, satha lakha vandu kara joda.
lines.translation_en: In each temple there are 180 images of Jinas. The total comes to 13,896,000,000 images. I pay homage with folded hands.

lines.transliteration: batrisase ne oganasatha, tirchha lokama chaityano patha; trana lakha ekanu hajara, tranase visa te bimba juhara.
lines.translation_en: In the middle world there are 3,259 Jain temples with 391,320 images in them. I pay homage to all.

lines.transliteration: vyantara jyotisima vali jeha, sasvata jina vandu teha; rsabha, chandranana, varisena, vardhamana name guna-sena.
lines.translation_en: In the regions of forest-dwelling gods (Vyantardeva) and luminous gods (Jyotishika Deva) there are innumerable temples. I pay homage to all the images of Jinas permanently located there, whose names are Rushabh, Chandranana, Varishena and Vardhmana.

lines.transliteration: sammeta-sikhara vandu jina visa, astapada vandu chovisa; vimalachala ne gadha giranara, abu upara jinavara juhara.
lines.translation_en: I pay homage to the 20 images on Sametashikhara, 24 images on Ashtapad mountain, and all the images on Shatrunjaya (Vimalachala), Girnara and Abu.

lines.transliteration: sankhesvara kesariyo sara, tarange sri ajita juhara; antarikkha varakano pasa, jiraulo ne thambhana pasa.
lines.translation_en: I pay homage to Lord Parshvanatha at Shankheshwara, Lord Ajitnatha at Kesariyaji and Taranga, Antriksha and Varkana Parshvanatha, Jiravala and Stambhana Parshvanatha.

lines.transliteration: gama nagara pura patana jeha, jinavara chaitya namu gunageha; viharamana vandu jina visa, siddha ananta namu nisa-disa.
lines.translation_en: I pay homage to all images in temples of villages, towns, cities and capitals of all provinces of Bharata; and every day I respect the 20 existing Tirthankaras of Mahavideha continent and the infinite perfected souls (Siddhas).

lines.transliteration: adhi dvipama je anagara, adhara sahasa silangana dhara; pancha maha-vrata samiti sara, pale palave panchachara.
lines.translation_en: I pay homage every morning to all the sages of two and a half islands who observe 18,000 restraints, 5 major vows, the fivefold path of vigilance (Samiti) and 5 categories of ethical behavior (Achara).

lines.transliteration: bahya abhyantara tapa ujamala, te muni vandu guna-mani-mala; nita nita uthi kirti karu, jiva kahe bhava sayara taru.
lines.translation_en: I bow to those monks who have practiced 6 external and 6 internal austerities and who are full of pious attributes like a string of precious stones. Says Jiv Vijay Maharaj: thus I will cross the ocean of mundane existence.

interpretation: With folded hands, this sutra pays obeisance to all the eternal and non-eternal Jina temples and images of the Tirthankaras, enumerating the vast numbers of Jina-temples across the twelve heavens, the nine Graiveyakas and the five Anuttara heavens. Reciting the names of the Jinas at each place is said to bring immeasurable merit.

title: Shree Savvassavi Sootra

lines.transliteration: Savvassa Vi Devasia, Duccintia, Dubbhasia,
lines.translation_en: For all sinful thoughts and words committed during the day,

lines.transliteration: Duccitthia
lines.translation_en: And for all sinful activities committed during the day,

lines.transliteration: Icchakarena Sandisaha Bhagavan
lines.translation_en: O Lord! With your permission, may I admit to all harmful activities committed during the day?

lines.transliteration: Iccham, Tassa Micchami Dukkadam.
lines.translation_en: I accept your permission. May all those harmful deeds be forgiven and become fruitless.

interpretation: This sutra seeks forgiveness for all harmful thoughts, words, and deeds committed during the day. With the guru's permission, the aspirant admits to all transgressions and prays for them to be forgiven and rendered fruitless.
